title: Make an Investing Starter Plan
blurb: Set goals and understand the tradeoffs before choosing investments.
cards: i
Start with your goal and timeline
Write down what the money is for and when you may need it. Money needed soon is usually less suited to investments that can change sharply in value.
i
Build a financial base first
Consider essential bills, costly debt and a cash buffer before taking investment risk. The right order depends on your circumstances and local rules.
i
Understand risk, costs and access
Learn what could make an investment lose value, what fees apply, how quickly you can access money, and whether the provider is regulated where you live.
q
You need money for a bill next month. What matters most?
Choose the most volatile investment
Keep the bill money accessible and avoid risking it
Invest it all for a quick gain
Borrow to invest
Short-term essential money generally needs reliability and access, not exposure to market swings.
t
Past performance guarantees an investment's future return.
Past performance cannot guarantee future returns.
q
Before using an investment platform, what should you check?
Only its social media followers
Its fees, risks, and regulatory status using official sources
A stranger's promise of fast profits
Whether it asks for your password
Research the provider and product using trusted, official information.
example: If you need money for a course fee in three months, a volatile investment could drop just when the bill is due. Keep near-term essential money accessible.
